cause: ParaView 5.13 is not set up as the Confluence page says (installed system-wide, its bin folder on PATH), so the Cerb-FF report cannot find pvbatch.
prove: The FF error mentions pvbatch or ParaView; compare the PATH entry with the Confluence setup page.
fix: Install ParaView 5.13 system-wide, put its bin folder (not pvbatch itself) on PATH, and restart.

cause: Zscaler or a certificate check blocks a package download, so Cerberus reports 'failed to download' and may not update.
prove: The error says 'failed to download' (torch in DSS-937); it happens on the office network or a hot desk.
fix: Follow the Cerberus 'failed to download' section of the Hot Desking Troubleshooting Guide; otherwise IT.

cause: Dropbox or VFS sync is stuck, so the Cerberus update never arrives or the wheel copy hangs.
prove: The reporter's last session runs a version older than prod, or the wheel copy hangs; Dropbox is still syncing.
fix: Let Dropbox finish or fix the sync, then relaunch Cerberus.

cause: Dropbox sits at its default folder under C:\Users instead of F:\DarkVision Dropbox, so Cerberus cannot find its files.
prove: The paths in the error or the session start with C:\Users\<user>\ and a Dropbox folder.
fix: Set the Dropbox location to F:\DarkVision Dropbox, then relaunch Cerberus.

cause: An Excel process left running by an earlier failed script blocks the COM server, so Cerberus loses its Excel connection.
prove: The error mentions the Excel or COM connection, and Task Manager shows a leftover Excel process.
fix: End the leftover Excel process in Task Manager and rerun.

cause: The client info is locked on the share, so Cerberus, MATLAB and Excel all fail to open it.
prove: Every tool fails on the same client info, Excel included.
fix: Close the client info wherever it is open; if nobody has it open, ask IT to clear the lock.

cause: Stage design names with commas, several dashes or other special characters break the fill scripts and plot saving.
prove: Read the stage design names in the client info; the failing step is a fill script or a plot save.
fix: Use a simple stage design name for now. Code fixes so far: DSS-845 changed the fill delimiter to semicolons; DSS-826 cleans the plot save path.

cause: The client info's version says 1.4 while its content follows 1.5, so Cerberus reads it with the wrong sheet map.
prove: Compare the version in the Dropdown sheet with the template the content follows.
fix: Set the version in the Dropdown sheet to match the content, then rerun.

cause: The cluster info sheet had spec depths in ft and found depths in m, so the volumetric calculation got an empty table and failed.
prove: Compare the units of the depth columns in the cluster info sheet.
fix: Fill the cluster info depths in the units the template expects, then rerun.

cause: An input file or folder is not named the way Cerberus expects, and Cerberus matches names exactly; MATLAB is laxer for some names.
prove: Compare the names with the convention: DVT<n>_ project folders, <pass>_Radial pass names and caliper files, the casing tally file name.
fix: Rename to the convention (copy old files first), then rerun.

cause: The RM names the perf randomizer reads do not match the perf info in the client info, so the randomizer errors.
prove: Run Check Names and compare the RMs it lists with the client info perf info.
fix: Correct the RMs so they match, then rerun.

cause: The LWP's final perforation bookmarks are empty (not finalized), so the alternative-well baselines come out NaN and Make Baseline Plots Only fails.
prove: Read the LWP project's final perforation bookmarks; they are empty.
fix: Finalize the LWP perforations, then rerun.

cause: The client info casing record ID differs from the casing tally, so the nominal thickness, and with it the wall loss, is off.
prove: Compare the casing record ID with the tally, and recompute the wall loss with each.
fix: Correct the casing record to match the tally, then rerun.

cause: A casing size change has no casingSplit in the client info (older templates lack the column), so the 2D log and Techlog treat the casing sizes wrongly.
prove: The casing record has more than one size and no casingSplit value at the change.
fix: Add casingSplit at the size change, using the current template, and rerun catcall. DTN-3717 tracks the split at a tiny depth gap seen in DSS-1225.

cause: The RADX config clips the RAID 2D log at 0 ft, so a clean range that starts at a negative depth is cut off.
prove: The clean range starts at a negative depth, and the RADX config's Depth Min is 0.
fix: Set Depth Min in the RADX config editor to the top of the clean range. DTN-3673 stops the clip at 0.

cause: A RADX render temp file path is over the Windows 260-character limit (262 in DSS-1229), so the RAID 2D log is not produced.
prove: Measure the temp page PDF path built from the project path.
fix: Shorten the project path for now; DTN-3727 is the code fix.

cause: A new release of a tool Cerberus depends on (VizApp, Napari, PySide6) changes its behaviour, so a Cerberus script breaks.
prove: The break started after that tool updated, and the error is inside the tool's API.
fix: Pin the version that worked, or update the Cerberus code and release a new wheel.
